notes:
Background: LucidCurio operates a 20+ year media archive (video + transcripts + legacy doc formats). Primary goal: fast retrieval for editorial tooling, content discovery and legal e-discovery.

POC scope / goals:
- Index scale target: ~30M-40M chunks (expecting ingest of 8M long transcripts; avg raw doc size 4k-12k tokens).
- End-to-end p90 latency goal for editor flow: <= 400ms; interactive goal <= 250ms for short queries.
- Cost target: ~$0.01-0.03 per query (vector retrieval + optional reranker).

Technical preferences & constraints:
- Prefer private deployment (on VPC) due to contractual residency requirements. On-prem for air-gapped legal case work.
- Need SSO/SAML and KMS integration; audit logs for every retrieval.

Chunking strategy discussion (notes from 2026-02-08 call):
- Lean toward variable chunk sizes: 512 tokens for short-form captions, 800-1,024 tokens for narrative transcripts and articles. Use sliding window with 128-token overlap on long transcripts to preserve context.
- Store original offsets & file-level metadata (show, date, speaker) in vector index to enable provenance.
- Prefer soft metadata filtering at retrieval time (genre, year, speaker) to reduce reranker load.

Embedding & index design:
- Two-tier retrieval: dense bi-encoder for top-200 recall + lightweight BM25 for initial filter. Aim to do dense top-200 then sparse filter to cut to top-50.
- Candidate embed models under consideration: open-embedding-large (higher recall) vs compact all-mpnet (lower cost). Running recall vs cost sweep.
- Quantized index (int8) + IVF+PQ on Faiss for storage efficiency; consider HNSW on Milvus for lower-latency tail.

Reranker tuning & architecture:
- Hybrid reranking: bi-encoder to retrieve high-recall set, then cross-encoder reranker for top-10 to maximize precision.
- Plan experiments on reranker size: distil cross-encoder (faster, ~80-120ms per item) vs medium cross-encoder (higher quality, ~250-350ms). Use cascade: cheap reranker to trim to top-20, heavy cross-encoder on top-5.
- Labeling: internal editorial relevance judgments (2k curated Q-A pairs) + synthetic hard negatives from anchor-chunk differences.
- Tuning knobs: temperature, length penalty on reranker scoring, query expansion heuristics for named-entity heavy queries.

Operational/POC milestones:
- Week 0-1: ingest pipeline (S3 -> transcription normalization -> chunker v0.1 with overlap).
- Week 2: embed batch runs on sample 2M chunks; measure embed throughput and storage.
- Week 3: run retrieval latency sweep (k=50,100,200) and reranker cascade experiments.
- Week 4: final configuration + cost per query modeling and handoff doc.

Quotes / call snippets:
- "We can't exceed 300ms in our editorial UI for the majority of queries" — Head of Product (2/8).
- "If we can get recall >95 on legal search with p95 latency under 1s, we will push to procurement" — Legal Ops.

Open risks & blockers:
- Security team requires private control plane for PII-containing transcripts — slows POC deployment.
- Unclear long-term budget for dedicated GPUs if heavy cross-encoder reranking required.

Internal notes for Redwood SE:
- Try Redwood Optimize suggestion: prefix-KV caching for recurring editorial queries; recommend quantization profile and hybrid routing to cheaper models for bulk background tasks.
- Evaluate fallback policy: if heavy reranker overloaded, return bi-encoder ranked response with provenance and soft confidence score.

Attachments referenced: pricing deck, security FAQ, sample ground-truth relevance set (drive links above).
